recaps.title: 2025 Season Review: Business as Usual in Edina
recaps.varsityHeadline: Varsity: 11 Wins, a State Berth, and One Very Awkward Afternoon at Edina Country Club
recaps.varsityBody:
The 2025 Edina Boys Golf season started the way most Edina seasons do — by immediately making other programs wonder why they scheduled this. A 283 (-5) at the Lake Conference Opener at Braemar set the tone on day one, followed two days later by a first-place finish at the East Ridge Invitational ahead of 15 other programs. April went exactly as planned: five events, five wins, including a dominant showing at the Border Battle Final where the Hornets topped 22 teams at St. Croix. Twenty-two.

May brought more of the same — right up until May 13, when Edina went 8th of 15 at the Sartell Invite at Blackberry Ridge. We're going to note that, acknowledge it happened, and move on at a brisk pace. Two days later came the CDH Duel at Edina Country Club. Their home. Their course. The one with their name on the sign out front. CDH won. We'll give them that one. The Hornets responded by winning their next three outings, because of course they did.

Leading the charge all season was Torger Ohe, whose 71.9 scoring average across 17 rounds was the kind of number that gets circled, underlined, and forwarded to opposing coaches as a professional courtesy. Low round of the year: a 67. His brother Sander wasn't far behind at 74.9 — making the Ohe household dinner table a fairly uncomfortable place for anyone who plays golf in the Lake Conference. Chase Larson and Peter Bennett each reached 69 at their best, anchoring the middle of a deep lineup with mid-74 averages all season long.

The postseason told the real story. Edina finished 2nd of 13 at the MSHSL 6AAA Section Tournament at Meadows at Mystic Lake — and while the team came up just short of advancing, two Hornets punched their individual tickets to state. Torger Ohe and Chase Larson both qualified for the MSHSL State Championship at Bunker Hills, competing against the best high school golfers in Minnesota. Torger finished T10th of 88 — a result that, on a course that asks hard questions in June, is about as good as it sounds.

Final record: 11 wins, 3 losses. Two individuals at state. The kind of season most programs would frame and hang in the lobby.
recaps.jvHeadline: JV: Podium Finishes, a Big Invite Win, and a Pipeline That's Clearly Wide Open
recaps.jvBody:
The JV squad had a season that deserves its own headline — and not just because they earned it.

The Hornets JV opened with back-to-back silver medals — 2nd of 7 at the Lake Conference JV Tournament at Bluff Creek and 2nd of 23 at East Ridge. Then things got comfortable: a first at the Rosemount JV Invite (1st of 10), and the signature result of the season — a 305 at the Eden Prairie JV Invite, good for 1st of 13. That's the kind of performance that puts a program on the map.

Macallen Smith turned in a 68 — the low round of the JV season — and Hudson Strodl put together a consistent eight-event run with a 76.4 average. Carter Ringle and Ryan Geyer were forces throughout, and by late May the JV lineup looked more like a problem than a depth chart.

Seven event wins on the year. Multiple top-two finishes at invitationals. The 2025 JV squad did everything a program needs its underclassmen to do. The varsity roster noticed.
recaps.closingLine: The 2026 season opens April 20 at Braemar. The rest of the Lake Conference has had all winter to prepare. Good luck with that.
